c.tagline: Red Sea gateway to Mecca, where a coral-stone old town meets the world's tallest fountain.

emergency.note: 999 police, 997 Red Crescent ambulance, 998 civil defense/fire, 993 traffic. English-speaking operators are usually available.

hood_landmark.Al Andalus: Tahlia Street (Prince Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Street), Jeddah

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpocketing in the crowded Al-Balad souq lanes and be very careful crossing roads — driving is aggressive.

hood_desc: Jeddah's UNESCO-listed old town, a warren of coral-stone tower houses with carved wooden balconies, souqs and historic mosques near the waterfront; suits culture-seekers and first-timers who want the city's soul on foot.

A breezy northern seafront district strung along the Corniche, with the landmark Floating Mosque, promenades, seafood restaurants and resort hotels; suits travelers wanting Red Sea views and sunset strolls.

A central, upscale corniche neighborhood facing the King Fahd Fountain, with luxury hotels, waterfront cafes and easy access to the old town; suits well-heeled visitors wanting polish close to the sights.
A modern inland district of malls, Tahlia-style dining and mid-range hotels; suits families and business travelers wanting contemporary comforts and shopping.

A modern commercial district inland of the Corniche, where Tahlia Street (Prince Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Street) meets Madinah Road, lined with shops, cafes and international-brand hotels; suits visitors who want upscale retail and dining rather than a seafront base.

water.note: Treated water meets standards, but bottled water is recommended, especially in older districts.

transit.pay: Jeddah has no metro yet, so most visitors rely on ride-hailing apps (Uber, Careem) and taxis. SAPTCO city buses take a rechargeable smart card or the app, with single fares of a few riyal; the Haramain High Speed Railway links Jeddah to Mecca and Medina from Sulaimaniyah station.
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6am-midnight; ride-hailing is available around the clock. The Jeddah Metro is still under construction.

transit.m: Haramain High Speed Railway to Jeddah (Sulaimaniyah), ~10 min
SAPTCO airport bus to city center, ~40 min

landmarks: King Fahd's Fountain

The world's tallest fountain shoots seawater over 260 meters into the sky above the Red Sea corniche, creating a dazzling spectacle especially when illuminated at night. It's Jeddah's unmistakable skyline signature.
Al-Balad (Historic Jeddah)

This UNESCO World Heritage old town is a maze of coral-stone buildings with intricately carved wooden balconies (rawasheen) that whisper centuries of trade history. Wandering its narrow alleys at dusk feels like stepping into another era.
Jeddah Corniche

A breezy waterfront promenade stretching for miles along the Red Sea, dotted with sculptures, cafes, and sunset viewpoints. It's the city's favorite spot to unwind and watch the sky turn gold over the water.
Al Rahma Mosque (Floating Mosque)

Perched delicately on stilts over the Red Sea, this white mosque appears to float on the water, especially magical at high tide or during prayer calls at sunset. It's one of the most photographed mosques in Saudi Arabia.
Jeddah Sculpture Museum (Open-Air)

Scattered along the corniche and major roundabouts, this outdoor collection features works by global modern artists like Joan Miró and Henry Moore, turning the entire city into an unexpected art gallery.
Fakieh Aquarium

A colorful family-friendly aquarium showcasing Red Sea marine life, from vibrant reef fish to sharks and turtles. It offers a fun, air-conditioned counterpoint to Jeddah's historic and coastal sights.
Naseef House

Once the tallest building in old Jeddah and a former royal guesthouse, this restored merchant mansion showcases classic Hejazi architecture with its grand wooden doors and shaded courtyards. It's a highlight of any Al-Balad walking tour.
King Abdulaziz Mosque
One of Jeddah's largest and most striking mosques, known for its soaring minaret and intricate geometric tilework. Its scale and craftsmanship make it a serene stop for architecture lovers.
Red Sea Mall & Jeddah Waterfront
Beyond shopping, this area offers striking modern architecture and lively evening promenades where locals gather for ice cream and sea views. It's a great snapshot of contemporary Jeddah life.
Al Shallal Theme Park

A lively seaside amusement park combining thrill rides with sweeping Red Sea views, popular for family outings and evening entertainment. Its Ferris wheel offers one of the best sunset panoramas in the city.

train.note: No international trains. The Haramain High Speed Railway links Jeddah (city centre and King Abdulaziz Airport stations) with Makkah, Madinah and King Abdullah Economic City at up to 300 km/h - the fastest way to reach the other holy cities.

intl.to: Egypt, the UAE, Bahrain & other Arab countries (SAPTCO network)

bus.note: SAPTCO's Jeddah bus station runs both domestic coaches across the Kingdom and an international network to neighbouring Arab countries. Bring your passport and confirm visa rules for any cross-border trip.

ferry.note: Jeddah Islamic Port is the Kingdom's main Red Sea harbour. Passenger sailings to Sudan and Egypt have historically run around Hajj and Umrah season but are irregular the rest of the year - confirm current schedules with a local agent before relying on one. Everyday cruise and cargo traffic otherwise dominates the port.

half.name: King Abdullah Economic City (KAEC)
half.blurb: A planned coastal development an hour north of Jeddah with beaches, a marina, and resort facilities.

full.name: Taif
full.blurb: A mountain city known for rose gardens and cooler air, reached by a two-hour drive up a winding escarpment road from Jeddah.

full.name: Al Wahbah Crater
full.blurb: A volcanic crater with a white salt flat at its base, about four hours inland from Jeddah.
